body:
feat(papercraft): real cross-platform CI -- client + map editor, Linux/Windows/macOS

Founder real-time: "make sure we have the proper clients uploading as artifacts" ->
"mac linux windows" -> "include the map editor".

New .github/workflows/ci.yml: a real Bazel test gate (bazel test //..., never run in
CI before this) followed by three platform build jobs -- Linux (native gcc), Windows
(mingw-w64 cross-compile, the same real pattern SHANKPIT's own release.yml already
proved), and macOS (native clang on macos-latest, Homebrew SDL2) -- each building
apps/client and apps/mapeditor and uploading the result via actions/upload-artifact.
apps/server deliberately excluded: it's Linux-only by design (runs on this monorepo's
own host, not a player's machine), matching SHANKPIT's own server/client CI split.

Real portability bugs found and fixed -- this was the first time apps/client was ever
compiled for anything but native Linux gcc:

- apps/client/src/main.c: the _WIN32 winsock2 include block came AFTER the GL/SDL
  includes; mingw's <GL/gl.h> drags in <windows.h> internally, so windows.h always won
  first and broke every winsock2-only symbol used below (plus a compiler #warning every
  build). Fixed by moving the _WIN32 socket-header block before any GL/SDL include.
- apps/client/src/main.c: added a real #if defined(__APPLE__) guard for
  <OpenGL/gl.h>/<OpenGL/glu.h> (macOS's own real path, deprecated-but-present, linked
  via -framework OpenGL) vs. <GL/gl.h>/<GL/glu.h> on Linux/Windows.
  Zero behavior change on Linux/Windows.
- apps/client/src/main.c: cast all 5 sendto() calls' packet-pointer argument to
  (const char *) -- winsock's own sendto takes const char*, not POSIX's const void*,
  so passing a struct pointer with no cast warns on Windows (harmless, but a real, cheap
  fix for a fully warning-clean cross-compile, not just a working one).
- packages/common/papercraft_worldobjects.h: pc_worldobjects_ensure_dir called POSIX
  two-argument mkdir(path, mode); Windows' own CRT mkdir (<io.h>) takes only a path.
  New PC_MKDIR macro (_mkdir on _WIN32, real mkdir(path, 0755) otherwise) hides the ABI
  difference behind one call site -- this header is pulled in transitively by
  apps/client (via papercraft_protocol.h), so it has to compile on Windows even though
  the client never calls this function itself.
  packages/common/papercraft_persist.h (server-only, apps/server's own real POSIX-only
  scope, documented in its own header comment) was deliberately NOT touched.

Verified:
- Raw-gcc (Linux) and raw-x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc (Windows, this repo's own already-
  installed cross toolchain, SDL2-devel-2.30.10-mingw fetched fresh from the real
  upstream SDL release) dry-runs of the exact commands the new workflow runs, for both
  apps/client and apps/mapeditor -- both link clean, zero warnings, zero errors, real
  working ELF/PE32+ binaries produced (confirmed via `file`).
- bazel clean && bazel build //... && bazel test //... after all fixes: 27 targets,
  12/12 tests pass, unaffected.
- The macOS job itself is NOT locally verifiable -- no macOS host in this environment,
  the same honest verification-tier limit named throughout this repo's own Phase
  1b/1c-client work; its first real run on GitHub's own macos-latest runner is the
  actual proof, not this commit.

Deliberately not attempted: release automation (auto-tag + GitHub Releases, matching
SHANKPIT's/PITVIPER's own "auto release non pre release" precedent) -- the real ask
was "uploading as artifacts," not "cut a release."

NORTHSTAR.md and README.md updated.
